clue.text: Where to stick brats in the workplace?

definitions.text: Where to stick brats in the workplace?

parts.note: surface reading: a grumpy hunt for somewhere to dump annoying children
setter's reading: the nursery an employer runs for staff's young children

explanation.surface: An exasperated parent wondering where at work to park the troublesome kids.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick' sounds dismissive, but the clue simply describes an office nursery.
explanation.definitionFit: A workplace nursery is where employees leave small children during working hours.

clue.text: Single? Get Cherry, perhaps, around — phwoar!

indicators.note: one thing placed around another encloses it

parts.note: cherry is a shade of red
both are British exclamations of admiration

explanation.surface: A lecher ogling someone called Cherry.
explanation.walkthrough: COR is a British exclamation of surprise or lust, like phwoar.
explanation.definitionFit: A single is a short release of one song, a type of disc or recording sold on its own.

clue.text: Tawdry Conservative, creepy character, reportedly, mounting sailor

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the sound counts here

parts.note: Uriah Heep is the creepy clerk in Dickens's David Copperfield
a jack, or jack tar, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A shabby Tory, slimy as Uriah Heep, climbing on top of a sailor.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'mounting' puts the earlier pieces on top of the sailor.
explanation.definitionFit: This old adjective describes cheap, shoddy goods, the stock of a hawker, and so means tawdry.

clue.text: Saying "Elizabeth's top gobbler" and stuff

indicators.note: the top of a down entry is its opening letter

parts.note: first letter
a pig gobbles its food
to ram is to cram or stuff

explanation.surface: A quotation calling the Queen the nation's greediest eater.
explanation.definitionFit: A short witty remark or pithy maxim is a saying of this kind.

clue.text: Withdraw whip in retaliation

parts.note: to back off or back out is to withdraw
a lash is a whip, or a stroke from one

explanation.surface: Pulling back the whip as a punishing response.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong hostile reaction against something counts as retaliation, a hitting back.

clue.text: 'Fat hip' Little Richard, a macho, cocky, number one dealer

definitions.text: a macho, cocky, number one dealer

parts.note: fat means large
hip and swinging both mean fashionable, as in the Swinging Sixties
the short, pet form of the name Richard

explanation.surface: A description of the rock'n'roll singer Little Richard as a swaggering ladies' man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little Richard' looks like the singer; 'Little' just asks for the pet form of the name.
explanation.definitionFit: This is City slang, popularised by Liar's Poker, for a top-earning, swaggering trader on a bond desk.

clue.text: Bill Labour's number one nit wrecked, getting protection of party

indicators.note: being protected by something means sitting inside it
something wrecked is broken up, so the letters come out in another order

parts.note: the three letters rearranged
CON is short for the Conservative party

indicators.note: the number one of a word is its first letter

parts.note: first letter

explanation.surface: A Labour leader being a wrecked idiot shielded by his party.
explanation.definitionFit: Bill is the first name of the former US president, so the surname completes it.

clue.text: Shag for example is out in the buff?

definitions.text: Shag for example is out in the buff?

parts.note: surface reading: sex; setter's reading: the shag, a seabird of the cormorant family, like the mythical bird that is a Merseyside city's emblem
setter's reading: the city's bird statues stand exposed high in the open air, as bare as a naturist

explanation.surface: A naked romp out of doors.
explanation.walkthrough: Liverpool's civic emblem is a cormorant-like bird, and the shag is one kind of cormorant; the second half of the clue is loose and its exact intent is unclear.
explanation.definitionFit: The shag is a cormorant, the species the Liverpool emblem is usually taken to depict.

clue.text: Did a Mick Jagger, shaking head and ass (wrinkly's butt)

indicators.note: shaking jumbles things up, so these letters are thrown into a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

indicators.note: a butt is the end, so only the final letter is kept

parts.note: last letter

explanation.surface: The ageing Rolling Stones singer wiggling his head and backside on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: A wrinkly is British slang for an old person.
explanation.definitionFit: Mick Jagger is famous for a swaggering, hip-swinging strut across the stage, a showy gliding walk.

clue.text: Having a shag in sun, being a deck hand?

parts.note: S is the standard abbreviation for sun
working as a sailor on a ship's crew

explanation.surface: A sailor enjoying a romp out on the sunny deck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shag' is British slang for having sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Screwing is vulgar slang for having sex, exactly what having a shag means in British usage.

clue.text: Lost your shirt? Play the stock market

definitions.meaning: first meaning, read as two words: wearing just your undershirt
second meaning: put money into shares

explanation.surface: Someone who has been ruined is told to gamble on shares.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lost your shirt' is an idiom for losing all your money, but here it literally means you are down to your vest, a British word for an undershirt.
explanation.definitionFit: To put money into stocks hoping for profit is the ordinary sense of the verb; split as 'in vest', it describes a shirtless man.

clue.text: One who feels good nuzzling up to cowboy?

parts.note: G is the usual abbreviation for good
a cowboy who lassoes cattle with a rope

explanation.surface: Someone getting cosy with a cowboy and feeling great about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feels good' reads as one phrase, but 'feels' ends the definition and 'good' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who paws or fondles others unwantedly is someone who feels them up.

clue.text: Such as Howe came to have of screwing Maggie?

definitions.text: Such as Howe came to have of screwing Maggie?

parts.words: Such as Howe came to have
parts.note: surface reading: a fantasy the Tory minister came to entertain
setter's reading: Howe was a 'wet', a moderate Tory, so his fantasy about Thatcher belongs to a wet

explanation.surface: A satirical jab at Geoffrey Howe's fantasies about Margaret Thatcher.
explanation.walkthrough: Geoffrey Howe was a Conservative minister under Margaret Thatcher (Maggie); Tory moderates she disliked were called 'wets'. 'Came' is a deliberate double meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: A nocturnal emission is an erotic sleeping fantasy, here punningly the fantasy of a political wet.

clue.text: Emasculated headcases, publicists!

indicators.note: emasculating removes the male, so the letter standing for male is taken away

parts.note: headcases are lunatics

explanation.surface: A jibe that advertising people are castrated lunatics.
explanation.walkthrough: M is the abbreviation for male; dropping it from MADMEN leaves ADMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Advertising executives promote products, so they work as publicists for their clients.

clue.text: One who gives head aggressively!

parts.note: surface reading: a sex act
setter's reading: someone who headbutts people, in slang 'nuts' them

explanation.surface: A crude picture of an over-vigorous oral sex partner.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'nut' someone is British slang for headbutting them, and the word also means a madman.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who headbutts, in British slang 'nuts', others is a violent head-giver, and such a person is typically a lunatic.

clue.text: Getting an erection makes belly whiff, note, internally

indicators.note: placed internally means put inside the other letters

parts.note: TUM is a childish word for stomach
a smell
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: Arousal leading to a smelly stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: Swollen and engorged describes an aroused penis, so the adjective fits becoming erect.

clue.text: Go soft and fluff — a disastrous failure

parts.note: melting is softening
down is soft fluffy feathers

explanation.surface: An embarrassing bedroom flop: going limp and fluffing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fluff' looks like a verb meaning to bungle, but it is the noun for soft feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: A reactor core overheating catastrophically gives the word, now used of any total collapse.

clue.text: Bloody hell! Labour encourages leaders to embarrass the Speaker

parts.note: a mild exclamation of annoyance

indicators.note: leaders are those at the front, so only the opening letter of each word is used

parts.note: opening letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Labour MPs swearing and egging each other on to humiliate the Commons Speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloody hell!' is a stronger version of the same oath, softened in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Interrupting a speaker with jeering comments discomfits them; capitalised Speaker is only surface disguise for anyone speaking.

clue.text: One can't get it from a good looker?

definitions.text: One can't get it from a good looker?

parts.note: surface reading: an attractive person
setter's reading: a malign glance that curses its target, which a well-meaning gazer would never give

explanation.surface: A wry complaint that you never get anything from beautiful people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good looker' is read as someone who looks at you with good intent.
explanation.definitionFit: A malevolent stare believed to bring harm can only come from someone looking with ill will, never a kindly gazer.

clue.text: Many religious followers' lives hit

parts.note: to live is to be, so 'lives' is 'is'
to lam is to beat or hit

explanation.surface: The lives of many religious believers being struck by misfortune.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition includes the possessive, with the answer taken as 'the faith's'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Muslim world, the community of its believers, is a vast body of religious followers.

clue.text: Expensive menu item? Chuck rest out

indicators.note: out here means out of order, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: to lob is to throw or chuck
the four letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A diner throwing out the remaining pricey items on the menu.
explanation.definitionFit: Shellfish of this kind is a famously costly restaurant dish, an example of a pricey course.

clue.text: Name one universal gay movement taking precedence in this country

indicators.note: movement shifts the letters around into a different order

parts.note: U is the film-certificate abbreviation for universal
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for name
a means one

explanation.surface: A country where the gay rights campaign leads the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking precedence' means the shuffled group goes before the letters from 'Name one'.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is a South American nation, the 'country' the clue points to.

clue.text: Shagging accepted by the "bird" at Christmas

definitions.meaning: first meaning: vulgar slang for having sex
second meaning: what is packed inside the festive turkey

explanation.surface: A seasonal romp, with 'bird' as British slang for a girlfriend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bird' in quotes hints at both a woman and the roast turkey.
explanation.definitionFit: The sage-and-onion filling goes inside the roast turkey, and the same word is crude slang for sex.

clue.text: Cover up, sweet

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to dodge or obscure the truth
second meaning: a soft confection made of sugar, butter and milk

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to evade or blur an issue, and the noun is a soft sugary confectionery.

clue.text: Row of tits on horseback

parts.note: slang for breasts, collectively a bust
a rider is said to be up

explanation.surface: A line of birds, or something ruder, riding horses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' rhymes with 'cow' here: a quarrel, not a line.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy quarrel or fight between people is a row in the British sense.

clue.text: Hard-on? Make love once, then wither

parts.note: 'make love' once meant to court, which is to woo
to wither away is to die

explanation.surface: An erection that comes after sex and then flags.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' signals the old-fashioned sense of 'make love', meaning courtship.
explanation.definitionFit: This is slang for an erection, being 'wood'.

clue.text: Time, during hernia operation, to get head of willy exposed

indicators.note: something happening during something else sits inside it
a surgical operation rearranges things, so these letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
T is the abbreviation for time

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter

parts.note: first letter

explanation.surface: A patient having his privates on show during hernia surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: A willy is British slang for a penis.
explanation.definitionFit: Being naked is being in the raw, with nothing covering the body, so the idiom means uncovered.

clue.text: Unthinking, has joint as well as Charlie

parts.note: the knee is a joint of the leg
a charlie is British slang for a fool

explanation.surface: Someone who smokes a spliff and takes cocaine too.
explanation.walkthrough: Joint and Charlie look like cannabis and cocaine; they are a body part and a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: A reflex reaction made automatically without reflection is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Talk to sailor about arse

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the joined words are read from end to start

parts.note: to gab is to chatter
a tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: Someone chatting to a seaman about bottoms.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are British insults for a contemptible, obnoxious person, so one is a fair synonym for the other.
